mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level at t-1mo predicts positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days by reducing discount rates applied to equity valuations, increasing present value of future cash flows, with the relationship holding across interest rate regimes.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level as predictor of 20-day returns remains below 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window, or correlation with returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals tight labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5% over 5-year rolling windows, or average return not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2% and CPIAUCSL inflation below 3% indicates a 'Goldilocks' economic environment that supports corporate profit growth and positive equity returns, while high inflation without growth signals negative returns.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when condition met is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in > 40% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: High real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above $700,000 million signals strong consumer demand that drives corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days during high-consumption regimes.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when RSAFS > 700000 is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in > 50% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 0.5% monthly growth signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings and positive equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when INDPRO growth > 0.5% is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in > 40% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.0%) combined with strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 0.5% MoM) indicates tight labor market and robust manufacturing, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when condition met is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in > 50% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) growth above 1.0% monthly signals strong consumer confidence in real estate, acting as a leading indicator for positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Average 5-day return when HOUST growth > 1.0% is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in > 40% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% over 3 months signals labor market strengthening that boosts consumer spending, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Average 60-day return when UNRATE decline > 0.2% in 3 months is negative or not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in > 50% of 3-year rolling windows.
